note: A four-bar song on A, D and E: one strum a bar, then a strum on every beat, then the same bars over a backing track. The key is the lesson (open chords), so moves holds only a tempo range, and the text leaves the chord order to the lit boxes.

exercise.title: A, D and E: a song in four bars
exercise.why: The song stays on A for two bars and goes to D and E for one bar each, so the long A is where your hand rests and gets ready for the two quick changes.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play. Strum down once on beat 1 and use the rest of the bar to move.
Practice until D and E are ready before their beat 1.

Press Play below to start the metronome. Play the same four bars with a down strum on every beat.
If a change comes late, keep your strumming hand going and catch the next beat 1.

Press Play below to start the backing track: drums and bass play the same four bars, and the lit chord box shows the chord. Strum down on every beat, and on the A bars try a down and an up strum on each beat.
Practice until you can look away from your fretting hand on the A bars.
